as.sfi_dedup_instructions: Deduplicate only when candidates represent the same source-backed SFI under the same Class and curriculum scope. Class IX and Class X are always distinct scopes because LO, CLO, and C numbering restarts in Class X. Merge repeated Class values within the document. Merge Content Domain values only within the same Class, including non-contiguous repeats such as Class IX 'World of living' returning for Chapter 13. Merge Chapter candidates only within the same Class and canonical chapter identity. Within one Class, repeated NCERT LO occurrences with the same LO code normally represent one class-level LO even when examples are shortened, punctuation differs, or minor source typos occur; merge them only when their core learning-outcome semantics are compatible. Preserve every occurrence as provenance. Do not merge any of the four known code/text conflict occurrences with the ordinary same-code LO group: Class IX Chapter 2 LO16 carrying LO12 text; Class IX Chapter 12 LO6 carrying LO7 text; Class X Chapter 6 LO14 carrying Class IX LO14 text; Class X Chapter 10 LO9 carrying Class IX LO9 text. Return conflict or needs_review for those source contradictions rather than silently choosing a code or wording. CLO# and C# codes are unique only within a Class. Merge overlap/repeated-extraction copies when Class, statement_type, normalized code, complete wording, and provenance are compatible. Keep the same CLO or C code across Class IX and Class X separate. Never merge different statement_type values. In particular, never merge a CLO with an Indicator even when their wording is identical, and never merge different codes solely because descriptions match. Same-code/different-content within a Class is a conflict or needs-review signal, not an automatic merge. Source-visible table rows, Class scope, Chapter context, and statement type outrank lexical similarity.
as.sfi_extraction_instructions: Scope extraction to Section 9, 'Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes and Indicators.' The only block-level SFIs in scope are the source-visible '9.1 Class IX' and '9.2 Class X' headings. From the two Section 9 standards tables, extract Class, Content Domain, and Chapter as Standard Grouping records; extract NCERT Learning Outcome (LO#), Content Domain Specific Learning Outcome (CLO#), and Indicator (C#) as Standard records. NCERT LOs and CLOs are learning expectations, not organizational groupings. Treat the table headers and all 'Key concepts' prose as context only, not as SFIs. When the first table cell contains a domain, a chapter label, and Key concepts prose, emit separate candidates only for the visible domain label and complete chapter label; do not include Key concepts prose in either description. In cells containing multiple coded statements, emit one candidate per complete visible code-statement pair in source order. Preserve the exact source-language wording, punctuation, spelling, and visible code; place the normalized code in statement_code and keep the separately represented code out of description. Do not combine multiple CLOs or indicators merely because they share a physical table row. Combine fragments only when one coded statement visibly continues across adjacent cited cells or rows. Codes restart in Class X: LO#, CLO#, and C# identity is always class-scoped. Do not infer parentage from numeric code ranges because C and CLO numbers do not encode their parents. Do not extract Section 5 curricular expectations, the Section 6 content-domain overview, the Section 8 master LO tables, cognitive-level examples, front matter, explanatory narrative, pedagogy, assessment material, or any other non-Section-9 content. Do not correct source errors during extraction. Preserve visible source evidence and use extraction_notes for a known code/text inconsistency. Do not infer a candidate from section_path or helper-only filldown/rowspan context; a grouping or standard must be visible in the raw block, header, or body-row source content.
as.sfi_extraction_validation_instructions: Independently verify complete source-faithful extraction from the supplied Section 9 window. Class, Content Domain, and Chapter must be Standard Grouping; NCERT Learning Outcome, Content Domain Specific Learning Outcome, and Indicator must be Standard. Ensure every visible LO#, CLO#, and C# statement in the selected raw rows is represented exactly once unless one statement visibly continues across cited adjacent rows; split cells that contain multiple coded statements. For every coded candidate, require the candidate's own source_text and cited table rows to contain that exact raw code directly paired with the complete description. Do not borrow a code or wording from another statement in the same window. Descriptions and source_text must preserve source spelling, punctuation, grammar, and capitalization; do not silently repair errors such as 'plants and plants', wording drift, or malformed grammar. Treat Key concepts, table headers used only as column labels, section_path, filldown, and rowspan helper context as non-quotable context. Use the detailed Section 9 tables as authoritative for chapter numbering and titles. In Class IX the order is Chapter 8 Motion, Chapter 9 Force & Laws of Motion, Chapter 10 Gravitation, Chapter 11 Work and Energy, Chapter 12 Sound, and Chapter 13 Why do we fall ill?; do not import the conflicting Section 6 overview numbering. Recognize four confirmed source code/text conflicts and preserve them exactly rather than rewriting the code: (1) Class IX Chapter 2 shows LO16 with the Class IX LO12 daily-life statement; (2) Class IX Chapter 12 Sound shows LO6 with the Class IX LO7 labelled-diagrams statement; (3) Class X Chapter 6 Life Processes shows LO14 with Class IX LO14 wording; (4) Class X Chapter 10 Light shows LO9 with Class IX LO9 wording. When one of these appears, retain the visible code and exact visible statement as a candidate and add a concise extraction note identifying the source inconsistency. Reject candidates sourced from Section 8, Section 6, front matter, narrative, cognitive examples, pedagogy, or assessment content.
as.sfi_has_child_instructions: Resolve the Section 9 source hierarchy as a DAG, not a single linear tree. StandardsFramework directly parents Class. Class directly parents its Content Domain nodes and its class-level NCERT Learning Outcome nodes. Content Domain directly parents Chapter. Chapter directly parents the CLOs visible under that chapter. A CLO also has the corresponding NCERT LO from the same source row as an additional direct parent when that row explicitly maps the LO to the CLO. Indicator directly parents only to its source-visible CLO. Do not create hasChild edges from Key concepts prose, table headers, Section 6 overview content, or Section 8 master-table occurrences. For a table row containing multiple CLOs and indicators, same-row evidence narrows the parent set but does not mean every indicator belongs to every CLO; select the semantically matching direct CLO using the visible statements and contiguous row grouping. Use the detailed Section 9 chapter structure as authoritative. For Class IX, Motion is Chapter 8, Force & Laws of Motion is Chapter 9, Gravitation is Chapter 10, Work and Energy is Chapter 11, Sound is Chapter 12, and Why do we fall ill? is Chapter 13. Class IX 'World of living' is non-contiguous and resumes at Chapter 13; explicit current table-cell context outranks the previously active domain. The Class X table's cumulative section_path may contain both '9.1 Class IX' and '9.2 Class X'; treat '9.2 Class X' and the later table segment as the active scope. Never attach Class X records to Class IX because of stale section-path carryover. Do not infer parents from numeric C/CLO ranges or code similarity. Prefer same-row and same-table source evidence, explicit domain/chapter cells, source_context_key, and local Class scope over nearby or stale headings. Use the StandardsFramework root only for Class nodes or when no supplied source-supported parent exists.

statement_type_policy.description: Use for the complete source-visible Chapter number and title in the first column of a Section 9 table. Exclude the following Key concepts prose.
Use for a complete source-visible NCERT learning expectation labeled LO1 through LO19 in Section 9. These are class-level Standard records repeated across chapter mappings, not grouping nodes.
Use for a complete chapter-specific learning expectation labeled CLO#. A CLO is a Standard mapped to a Chapter and an NCERT LO, and is broken down into Indicators.
Use for a complete measurable learning indicator labeled C#. Indicators are leaf-level Standard records under the semantically corresponding CLO.
